question.text: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) collectively currently hold net long positions of INR 35 billion in exchange-traded interest rate futures (IRF). Up to what additional net long amount (in INR billion) can FPIs collectively add before hitting the RBI-prescribed collective limit?

answer.text: INR 15 billion — the FPI collective net-long IRF limit is INR 50 billion, and 50 - 35 = 15
INR 50 billion — the INR 50 billion limit applies per contract, not overall
INR 65 billion — as the limit is calculated on a gross basis, not net
There is no limit; FPIs collectively have unlimited net long capacity in IRF

explanation.text: The Logic: RBI has prescribed an aggregate cap of INR 50 billion on the collective net long position of FPIs in IRF. With FPIs collectively net long INR 35 billion, the headroom is 50 - 35 = INR 15 billion before the limit is reached. The Trap: The INR 50 billion is a collective FPI net-long ceiling, not a per-contract limit and not unlimited; it is measured on a net long basis, not a gross basis. Note: This limit applies to FPIs as a class. It is distinct from any participant-specific or product-specific position limits.
